body: The spec's core drift model contradicts the project idea it is supposed to specify. The research plan fits an exponential decay, drift(t) = a·exp(−b·t) + c, and expects representational distance to *decline* over training ('systematic reduction in representational distance... reflecting consolidation'). But FR-005 mandates a linear *divergence* model, drift(t) = a + b·t, and defines DriftRate as 'the linear rate of increase in representational distance over time (divergence)'. These are not equivalent parameterizations: b has different meaning, sign, and units in each, so the synthetic ground-truth validation in SC-001 ('decay parameter... within 5% error') cannot test the model actually specified in FR-005. The spec must pick one model (and one definition of drift magnitude — the idea's 'mean off-diagonal distance' vs. the spec's per-time-point fit) before any validation tolerance is meaningful. Separately, FR-003 requires excluding 'performance-modulated neurons (e.g., error-related firing)', which risks excluding precisely the plasticity signal the project seeks — learning-related firing changes are performance-related by definition, so the exclusion criterion needs an operational definition or it will silently gut the drift metric. Finally, the underlying dataset is still a placeholder ('ds004xxx'), so Assumption about data availability (N ≥ 15 subjects with matched spikes and behavior) is asserted, not established.
